contentBlocks.text: This week you've learned dialogue, character, and dramatic irony. Today: analyze one complete scene using all three!

Read this complete scene: (The audience has seen TOMAS hide a surprise party invitation.) MAYA: (checking her watch) It's fine. We have plenty of time. TOMAS: (glancing at his bag) You've checked that watch four times in two minutes. MAYA: Have I? I hadn't noticed. Why do you keep checking your bag, anyway? TOMAS: No reason. Just making sure I have everything. Write a short paragraph analyzing this complete scene: what do the stage directions and dialogue reveal about each character, and how does dramatic irony add tension?
You just wrote a complete dramatic analysis! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Combine dialogue analysis, character inference, and dramatic irony into one written analysis
Write a coherent paragraph analyzing the complete MAYA/TOMAS scene
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's dialogue, character, and dramatic-irony work together.
2. Read the complete combined scene together.
3. Have the child write their full analysis paragraph.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: have the child answer three separate guiding questions (What does MAYA's behavior reveal? What does TOMAS's behavior reveal? What does the audience know that they don't?) before combining them into one paragraph
Ready for more: ask the child to predict what might happen in the scene right after this one, based on the tension already built
This is the week's synthesis moment — combining all three techniques into one coherent written analysis is the genuinely important skill here
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended analysis activity — check that the paragraph identifies MAYA's anxiety (shown through watch-checking despite her denial), TOMAS's own secret nervousness (shown through his own bag-checking), and explains that dramatic irony (the audience knowing about the hidden invitation) creates tension as the audience watches both characters act suspiciously without knowing the full picture.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 9-10 RL.9-10.3/RL.9-10.4/RL.9-10.5 together, synthesizing this week's three drama-analysis techniques before tomorrow's review.
